name: MO-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean makes this a safely Republican seat
Prediction markets price the Republican near 94%
Stigall's roughly 8-to-1 fundraising edge over Smead
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but not the underlying lean
model.rationale: The district's nineteen-point Republican lean, Stigall's dominant fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 94% Republican all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat; the modest outside spending against Stigall is far too small to signal a genuine contest.
model.watch: New polling or a large influx of Democratic outside spending showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's sixth district is one of the most Republican seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly nineteen points to the right. Sam Graves's retirement puts an open seat on the ballot, but the fundamentals still favor the GOP. Republican Chris Stigall has raised about $599,000, while Democrat Josh Smead has brought in roughly $72,000, and outside groups have spent about $138,000 opposing Stigall, a modest sign of Democratic interest but far from a serious investment. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 94% chance of winning.

No public polls cover the race, so the forecast rests on the district's lean, fundraising, and market pricing. A Libertarian candidate appears on the ballot, which could shave a point or two off the Republican margin in a low-information race. The expected outcome is a double-digit Republican hold, with residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
